response.sql:
WITH high_rate_fees AS (
  SELECT 
    f.orderslink,
    o.dealedge,
    (f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS net_fee_rate
  FROM fees f
  INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
  WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009
),
group_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    orderslink,
    dealedge,
    AVG(net_fee_rate) AS group_avg_net_fee,
    COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM high_rate_fees
  GROUP BY orderslink, dealedge
),
side_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    dealedge,
    AVG(group_avg_net_fee) AS side_avg
  FROM group_stats
  GROUP BY dealedge
)
SELECT 
  g.orderslink,
  g.dealedge,
  g.group_avg_net_fee,
  g.record_count,
  (g.group_avg_net_fee - s.side_avg) AS difference
FROM group_stats g
JOIN side_averages s ON g.dealedge = s.dealedge
WHERE g.group_avg_net_fee > s.side_avg
ORDER BY difference DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The phrase '0.0009 as the cutoff' for 'high-rate fee records' is interpreted as feerate > 0.0009 (strictly greater than), based on the term 'high-rate' implying records above the threshold.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff 0.0009 could be inclusive, meaning feerate >= 0.0009 instead of strictly greater than.
